Reproduced as printed. Sentence (5) cites Table 9.23.11.4.-C, which is not printed. Table -A has no row for 0.80 < Smax ≤ 1.2.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Joints in the top plates of loadbearing walls are staggered not
less than one stud spacing.
(a) one stud spacing where the number of nails required by Sentence (5)
is not more than 16, (b) two stud spacings where it is greater than 16
and not more than 32, and (c) three stud spacings where it is greater
than 32.
Top plates in loadbearing walls are lapped or otherwise tied at
corners and intersecting walls in accordance with Sentence (4).
Joints in single top plates used with loadbearing walls are tied in
accordance with Sentence (4).
Ties are the equivalent of not less than 75 mm by 150 mm by 0.91 mm
thick galvanized steel nailed to each wall with at least three 63
mm nails.
Except as provided in Sentence (7), doubled top plates in braced
wall bands are fastened on each side of a splice with not less than
76 mm long common steel wire nails or spiral nails, to the number
required by Table 9.23.11.4.-A or 9.23.11.4.-C, whichever is
greater, where
(a) Smax for Site Class C is greater than 0.47 and not greater than 2.6,
or (b) the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is equal to or greater
than 0.6 kPa but not greater than 1.2 kPa.
These nails are spaced not less than 75 mm o.c. along the top plate
in rows spaced not less than 35 mm apart.
Doubled top plates in braced wall bands are designed to Part 4
where
(a) HWP is greater than 1.2 kPa, (b) Smax is greater than 2.6, or (c)
Smax is greater than 0.47 for Site Class C for buildings of 3 storeys in
building height and (i) of heavy weight construction, (ii) clad with
masonry veneer, or (iii) clad with stone veneer (see Sentence
